A_general.open_code_note: Official legacy local stdio server: Make documents "Make Local MCP Server (legacy)" as npm package @makehq/mcp-server (https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/make-local-mcp-server-legacy.md); its source is github.com/integromat/make-mcp-server (Integromat is Make's former company name). It exposes on-demand scenarios as tools and is not the hosted server at mcp.make.com; its tools are not added to actions. The hosted server code is not public.
other_official_servers: MCP toolboxes: dedicated Make-hosted servers with selected scenario tools, unique URLs, API-key access, configurable labels/descriptions and read/read-write annotations; a distinct product from the global endpoint. https://help.make.com/mcp-toolboxes

Legacy Make Cloud MCP server documentation describes regional SSE endpoints; the current Make MCP server documentation describes stateless Streamable HTTP. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/make-cloud-mcp-server.md

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Scenario-run tools are available on all Make plans. Management tools require a paid plan. No separate MCP fee or per-call MCP price was found. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing page lists Free at $0/month with up to 1,000 credits/month; Core at $12/month, Pro at $21/month, and Teams at $38/month for 10,000 credits/month; Enterprise is custom priced. https://www.make.com/en/pricing
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Make charges by credits: each module action in a scenario generally counts as a credit, with AI-related exceptions. MCP scenario executions invoke the configured scenario and its modules; no separate MCP-call charge was identified. https://www.make.com/en/pricing ; https://help.make.com/credits
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Scenario-run tools expose active, on-demand scenarios. OAuth scopes determine available tools; API-key scenario access can be narrowed by organization, team, or scenario query parameters (those levels cannot be combined). OAuth connects to one selected organization; API-key scenario access defaults to active, on-demand scenarios across organizations. Management tools require a paid plan. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/connect-using-api-key/scenarios-as-tools-access-control
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Make controls plan-based availability and server behavior; the user selects OAuth scopes or API-key scopes, and API-key users can set documented scenario filters. Organization/team access also depends on Make permissions. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/connect-using-oauth ; https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/connect-using-api-key/scenarios-as-tools-access-control

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Exposes scenario-run tools and account-management tools. The available tool set depends on granted scopes, plan, organization access, and configured scenarios. Official documentation directs clients to tools/list or client settings to discover actual names, descriptions, and schemas; it publishes no fixed official tool-name list.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Scenario tools use scenario inputs as parameters and return configured scenario outputs. Timed-out scenario calls can return an executionId for later result retrieval. Management tool result schemas are not published in the reviewed documentation.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Official Make docs describe Make account resources and scenario outputs, but do not establish whether the input MCP endpoint implements the MCP resources capability. A third-party live inspection reports one resource, but its identity and relevance to this endpoint were not verified.
Official documentation does not describe MCP prompts on the server. A third-party inspection says the server declares prompts, but no prompt definitions were available to review.
Make says tool runs are visible in Make. The reviewed material does not specify what MCP request details are logged, how long MCP-specific logs are retained, or whether logging can be disabled.
No official documentation found describing MCP sampling support.
No official documentation found describing MCP roots support.

The supplied endpoint response is HTTP 401 and advertises Bearer resource metadata at https://mcp.make.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. That document names https://www.make.com/mcp as the authorization server and supports the bearer header. The supplied authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code and refresh_token grants, S256 PKCE, DCR at https://www.make.com/oauth/v2/register/mcp, token and revocation endpoints, and client_secret_post authentication at token/revocation endpoints. No scopes_supported or token-lifetime values appear in the supplied metadata. OIDC discovery returned 404. Make docs also describe API-key connection methods.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc / Dynamic Client Registration / OAuth / API key. Supplied metadata: bearer_methods_supported=["header"]; authorization_servers=["https://www.make.com/mcp"]; grant_types_supported=["authorization_code","refresh_token"]; code_challenge_methods_supported=["S256"]; registration_endpoint="https://www.make.com/oauth/v2/register/mcp"; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=["client_secret_post"]; revocation_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=["client_secret_post"]. scopes_supported is absent from the supplied metadata. Token lifetime not stated. Revocation endpoint: https://www.make.com/oauth/v2/revoke.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No official documentation found describing MCP Elicitation. The OAuth consent screen and client-side tool permission prompts are documented, but are not evidence of server-enforced MCP Elicitation.
Documentation describes a scenario timeout and a way to retrieve a completed run by executionId; it does not identify MCP Tasks support.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: A timed-out scenario can continue running for up to 40 minutes; the timeout response includes an executionId for later output retrieval using a corresponding tool.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: API-key scenario tools can be filtered by organizationId, teamId, or scenarioId; multiple values are supported for a given filter, but filter levels cannot be combined. maxToolNameLength can be set from 32 to 160 characters; default is 56. OAuth users select organization and scopes.
The reviewed sources describe timeout behavior but do not specify MCP error object formats, error reporting tools, or a server-side error reporting capability.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Timeouts may return an executionId and instruction text; other error structures not published.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No official documentation found describing MCP subscription notifications.
Scenario runs can continue after the client-facing call times out and later be retrieved by executionId; official docs do not identify MCP progress notifications.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: See the documented timeout response and executionId workflow under Tasks.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No MCP request cancellation mechanism is documented. Scenario deactivation appears in a third-party tool listing but does not establish cancellation of a running MCP request.
Official docs specify stateless Streamable HTTP. They also document generated tool-name length configuration and separately distributed Make Skills that provide setup and Make-specific instructions.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. Read/write: official docs describe scenario execution and account management that can modify scenarios, connections, webhooks, data stores, teams, and organizations. No official fixed tool list or annotations for this endpoint were found. Toolboxes separately allow read-only/read-write annotations; default is read/write. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://help.make.com/mcp-toolboxes
2. Server-enforced confirmation: no MCP-side confirmation workflow was found in official docs. Client consent and client permission prompts are described; they are not shown to be server-enforced confirmation. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/connect-using-oauth ; https://help.make.com/get-started-with-make-mcp-server
3. OAuth scopes govern tool access; OAuth connects to a selected organization. Scenario-run scope includes active on-demand scenarios; management scopes provide account management and are paid-plan only. API-key scenario tools can be filtered by organization, team, or scenario. Role inheritance, token lifetime, redirect URI approvals, and allowlists: Unknown. Supplied OAuth metadata has DCR and S256 PKCE, but no scopes_supported. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/connect-using-api-key/scenarios-as-tools-access-control
4. Restrictions: API-key scenario filters and maxToolNameLength are documented. OAuth permits selection of one organization. No read-only mode or general tools/toolsets filter is documented for the global endpoint. Scenario tools require active scenarios with on-demand scheduling. Make toolboxes are separate servers for selected toolsets. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://help.make.com/mcp-toolboxes
5. Data protection: no MCP-specific PII masking, field exclusion, or secret redaction behavior found. Scenario inputs and outputs determine exchanged data. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server
6. Limits: OAuth scenario-run timeout 25 s and management timeout 30 s; API-key scenario-run timeout 40 s and management timeout 60 s. Timed-out scenarios may continue up to 40 minutes and return executionId. Scenario plan execution limits and credit consumption apply. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://www.make.com/en/pricing
7. Validation/correction: scenario input/output definitions supply parameters; no MCP-specific unknown-argument handling, coercion, alias rewriting, or operator-overrides documented. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server
8. Monitoring/logging: Make says tool runs are visible in Make. MCP-specific audit fields, retention, telemetry, and opt-out: Unknown. https://help.make.com/introduction-to-mcp
9. Vendor-interest mechanisms: no feedback/rating/survey tool is apparent in the 67 names published by Claude's third-party connector listing. Docs recommend Make scenario descriptions to improve agent reliability; no upsell result or marketing elicitation found. https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/make ; https://developers.make.com/mcp-server
10. Behaviour shaping: Make Skills are Markdown instructions installable in MCP clients; docs recommend detailed scenario descriptions for more reliable calls. No server-provided initialize instructions were found. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://skills.make.com/
11. Memory/state: no agent-history-dependent behavior documented. Scenarios and Make account configuration define available tools and effects. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server
12. Structure: global server exposes scenario-run and management capabilities; tool set varies by scopes, plan, organization, and scenarios. Separate toolboxes offer dedicated scenario sets. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://help.make.com/mcp-toolboxes
13. Escape hatch: the third-party listing includes rpc_execute, but provides no schema or description sufficient to establish whether it is a general raw API escape hatch. https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/make
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: [DOCS] “Write detailed scenario descriptions to help MCP clients understand what each scenario does and get more reliable results.”
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The server exposes tools dynamically from the user's active on-demand scenarios in addition to scope- and plan-dependent management tools; its available toolset is not a single fixed list. Separate MCP toolboxes provide scenario-specific servers but are distinct from this endpoint.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Make advises: “Write detailed scenario descriptions to help MCP clients understand what each scenario does and get more reliable results.” The docs present this as guidance for scenario authors; no enforcement is described. Make Skills are optional client-installed Markdown instructions. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://skills.make.com/
F_documentation.governance_promises: Make describes MCP as enabling “safe interactions” and says the server connects to Make resources so clients can perform actions. Docs describe scope selection and scenario-level API-key filters; no MCP-specific promises about PII masking, AI training, data retention, or reversibility were found. https://developers.make.com/mcp-server ; https://developers.make.com/mcp-server/connect-using-api-key/scenarios-as-tools-access-control
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Make states that tool runs are visible in Make and that scenario/tool outputs are defined by the scenario author. https://help.make.com/introduction-to-mcp ; https://developers.make.com/mcp-server
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Scope selection and API-key filters are documented access controls; scenario timeouts and deferred result retrieval are documented runtime behavior. Visibility of tool runs is claimed, but logging details and retention were not specified. Guidance about detailed scenario descriptions is not described as enforced by the server. No source establishes initialize instructions or MCP-side confirmation.

contradictions: The official Make docs state tool names and schemas depend on scopes and scenarios and instruct users to inspect tools/list; Claude's third-party connector page lists 67 names, while Manufact reports 133 tools in its live inspection. These may reflect different configurations, client views, or inventory methods; no official fixed total resolves the discrepancy.

The input URL is the root https://mcp.make.com/ and its pre-fetched probe returns HTTP 401. Official Make docs specify https://mcp.make.com/v2 as the OAuth connection URL. The root probe establishes authorization metadata but does not establish that the root path itself serves MCP requests.

The provided protected-resource metadata has no scopes_supported value, while Make docs describe scope-selected tools and name scenario scopes such as scenarios:read. The supplied metadata therefore does not enumerate scopes or directly document the full permission set.

The official docs describe stateless Streamable HTTP for the current server; the older Make Cloud MCP server page describes SSE and older regional endpoint paths. The older page identifies itself as outdated.

The OAuth authorization server metadata names issuer https://www.make.com/mcp, while the endpoint's protected-resource metadata names that same authorization server; OIDC discovery at the supplied path returned 404.
observations_for_research: The server's tool inventory is partly user-authored: scenarios become tools when active, configured for on-demand scheduling, and supplied with scenario inputs/outputs.
Tool availability combines OAuth scope or API-key scope with plan eligibility and scenario configuration; management tools require a paid Make plan while scenario-run tools are offered on all plans.
The API-key method documents URL-level organization/team/scenario scoping; OAuth documentation describes organization and scopes, but not equivalent scenario-level OAuth filtering.
Make separates unrestricted account MCP access from MCP toolboxes, which expose selected scenarios through distinct endpoints and keys.
A scenario can continue running after the client-facing tool call times out, with later output retrieval via executionId.
